I just discovered that if I hold shift and select text, then I can copy manually. Hope this helps someone.

### Root Cause

The markdown agent files in `~/.config/opencode/agents/` used **invalid `color` values** in their frontmatter.

The V2 schema expects a **six-digit hex color** (e.g. `#3b82f6`), but all files used semantic/named values like `info`, `accent`, `warning`, `success`, `error`, and `secondary`. This caused the auto-discovery scanner to silently skip those files, making the agents invisible to the service despite valid `mode`, `model`, and `permissions`.

### Fix

Changed every `color` value from named semantics to proper hex:

| Agent | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| subagent1 | `info` | `#3b82f6` |
| subagent2 | `accent` | `#f59e0b` |
| subagent3 | `warning` | `#eab308` |
| subagent4 | `success` | `#22c55e` |
| subagent5 | `secondary` | `#6b7280` |
| subagent6 | `error` | `#ef4444` |

After the fix, `opencode2 api get /api/agent` returns all agents, and they can be invoked via `@mention` and the `subagent` tool.

### Prevention

The V2 docs explicitly require hex: https://v2.opencode.ai/docs/agents#color

> Use a six-digit hex color such as `#ff6b6b`.

Named CSS colors or semantic tokens are not supported in the `color` field. If auto-discovery ever silently skips markdown agent files again, checking the frontmatter against the [agents docs](https://v2.opencode.ai/docs/agents) should be the first step.
Closed by pyforgedev - root cause was invalid non-hex color values in markdown agent frontmatter. See comment above for details.
